arguments.text: Plan (min 1): 10 km, ~55 min, so race at about critical power (shaft ~160-165 W, boat ~100-103 W); hard start is normal, let it settle by min 3. Watches set: overpace, underpace, drag (push_local well below push_along = weed/drag?), pod_fail, reserve_low, finish_plan at 1600 m left. Early push_along -0.18 (against on leg 1, should help on the way back). Trust pod over boat-speed numbers if they disagree.

text: no cue: hard start is normal and should settle; set watches for pacing, drag, pod failure, low reserve and the finish, and noted the plan.

arguments.text: Good start. Settle now, ease a touch to race pace.
Min 4: still 175 W shaft vs 164 sustainable, pod reserve 71% and draining (boat reserve 60%). Cued a small ease (no pace target). Check next wake-up that shaft settles near 160-165 W and not lower.

text: Cued a small ease: shaft power 7% above what lasts to the finish and reserve draining at minute 4.

arguments.text: Min 7: settled at 164 W shaft = sustainable; pod reserve 64%, boat reserve 53%. Boat/pod power ratio slid 0.65 (min 3) to 0.61 (min 7); speed at same rate -3%. Added boat_eff metric + eff_drop watch (<0.56) to catch weed/drag. Turn at 1250 m now.

text: no cue: settled at sustainable power after the ease; added a boat-power-per-pod-watt metric and watch to catch drag such as weed.

arguments.text: Min 10 (1.8 km, leg 2 with current helping +0.19): shaft 167 W (sustainable 163), pod reserve 57%, no fade (+0.2%). Boat reserve 30% is current-contaminated, ignore it. Paddler says effort 3/10, plenty left: hint that tested CP (159 shaft) is low. Plan: ask again ~min 14-16; if still <=5/10 with no fade while pod reserve falls below ~45%, raise cp_shaft ~8% and cue a small push.

text: no cue: on sustainable pod power, no fade; paddler reports 3/10, so gathering more evidence that critical power is set too low before pushing.

arguments.text: Nice and steady. Back off a hair, long way to go.

Min 13 (2.4 km): shaft crept up to 170 W vs sustainable 163, pod reserve 47%, no fade. Paddler 4/10 (was 3/10 at min 10), says plenty: a rise like that fits on-pace effort building, so not strong evidence CP is low. Boat/pod ratio is higher on the south legs (current fit off), so boat reserve (12%) is unreliable. Cued a small ease. Next evidence: if pod reserve falls below ~15% with no fade and effort still moderate, raise cp_shaft.

text: Cued a small ease: pod power had crept 4% above what lasts to the finish with the pod reserve under half.
